## Solution

**Computing P(n).** The product inside the sum is

$$\prod_{k=0}^{n}\frac{1}{m+k} = \frac{1}{m(m+1)\cdots(m+n)}.$$

Using the telescoping identity

$$\frac{1}{m(m+1)\cdots(m+n-1)} - \frac{1}{(m+1)(m+2)\cdots(m+n)} = \frac{(m+n)-m}{m(m+1)\cdots(m+n)} = \frac{n}{m(m+1)\cdots(m+n)},$$

we get

$$\frac{1}{m(m+1)\cdots(m+n)} = \frac{1}{n}\left[\frac{1}{m(m+1)\cdots(m+n-1)} - \frac{1}{(m+1)\cdots(m+n)}\right].$$

Summing over $m=1,2,\dots$ the series telescopes; all terms cancel except the $m=1$ first piece, giving

$$P(n) = \frac{1}{n}\cdot\frac{1}{1\cdot2\cdots n} = \frac{1}{n\cdot n!}.$$

**Computing 1/P(k).** Thus

$$\frac{1}{P(k)} = k\cdot k!.$$

**Computing Q(n).** Since $k\cdot k! = (k+1)! - k!$,

$$Q(n) = \sum_{k=1}^{n}\bigl[(k+1)!-k!\bigr] = (n+1)! - 1! = (n+1)!-1.$$

So

$$Q(2015) = 2016! - 1,\qquad Q(2015)+2015 = 2016! + 2014.$$

**Last 4 digits.** Since $2016!$ contains far more than four factors of $2$ and four factors of $5$, it is divisible by $10^4 = 10000$, i.e. $2016!\equiv 0\pmod{10000}$. Therefore

$$Q(2015)+2015 \equiv 0 + 2014 \equiv 2014 \pmod{10000}.$$

The last 4 digits are $\boxed{2014}$.
